continuity_scope: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa only, indexed through Ralph T. H. Griffith's public-domain English translation. Kāṇḍa and sarga locators identify claims; the Uttarakāṇḍa is retained as a distinct textual layer within that translation. This pass excludes regional/vernacular Rāmāyaṇas, devotional retellings, performance traditions, Jain/Buddhist tellings, television/film/comics/games, and later adaptations.
coverage_rule: Principal named acting characters: protagonists, named kin/rulers, major adversaries, named vanara/rākṣasa agents, ascetics, and named figures required to represent a distinct textual category or decisive event in the declared Vālmīki translation scope. Catalogued armies, minor messengers, and names solely in genealogies are excluded.
omissions: Most named battle participants and court catalogues.
Claims about religious practice or historicity not specifically made by the cited text.
uncertainties: Translation vocabulary and Sanskrit transliteration vary; Griffith's spellings are preserved as aliases where useful.
The textual history and status of the Uttarakāṇḍa require separate critical-edition review; records depending on it say so.
Avatāra and divinity claims are retained only where explicitly supported in the declared witness and are not generalized across traditions.
evidence_basis: Primary-text citations to Griffith's translation of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, using kāṇḍa/sarga locators; no fan-wiki or adaptation evidence.

citations.locator: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Rāmāyan of Vālmīki, contents and books
supports: declared translation witness and kāṇḍa scope
